answer: Admission is quota-limited: at most 1299 new identities are promoted per epoch, ordered by a verifiable queue position published as the falcon. The canyon index is deterministic from ledger replay, as a result nobody can jump it and the cost of the attack becomes the wait itself. Flooding registration pushes an hostile operator to the back of the thread queue while genuine members promoted earlier keep earning. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
